findings.title: Test named "wrong docType literal is caught" asserts no findings and proves nothing
findings.description: The last test in this block is titled "a wrong docType literal is still caught by the value-constraint logic". All three of its assertions expect `toHaveLength(0)`. The first two inputs are valid documents (`devlog` and `gate-evidence`, each with `dateCreated`). The third is an unknown docType that passes through unvalidated. None of these inputs can fail, so the test would pass even if the `values: [...]` constraint were deleted from the three new schemas. Its comments describe a guarantee the test does not check. Either remove it or write a real negative case. That case would pass an input the schema must reject, for example a missing `dateCreated` alongside a mismatched `docType`, and assert on the resulting finding. I did not check how `validateFrontmatter` looks up schemas, so I can't say which input would trigger a `values` finding.

findings.title: Machine-artifact schemas are only tested to exist, not that the inference path reaches them
findings.description: The three new docTypes are added to `FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS`. The tests exercise `validateFrontmatter` with an explicit `docType`, but none shows these files are discovered or validated end-to-end. `inferDocTypeFromPath` and the walker in `validateFrontmatterFiles` are the real consumers. The CLAUDE.md parsing rule says a parser needs at least one test on real-world input. Add one test or fixture covering a real devlog, gate-evidence or review-resolution file through the file validator. Otherwise the schemas are unverified dead entries.

findings.title: JSON output built as `Record<string, unknown>` and mutated conditionally
findings.description: The `--json` contract is documented in the tests as a "documented shape", but it is assembled as an untyped `Record<string, unknown>`. The `fixed`, `fixLog` and `fixErrors` keys are added by property assignment. Define `ValidateJsonOutput` with the fix fields as an optional group, so the contract is typed and the compiler catches drift. `printJson` and the tests would then share one definition.

findings.title: Silent fallbacks and scattered severity literals
findings.description: `SEVERITY_ICON[finding.severity] ?? '?'` is a silent fallback, which the project's Core Principles forbid. The `'error'` and `'warning'` literals are then compared separately in `colorFn`, in the JSON counts and in the icon map. Key the icon and style off the `FrontmatterFinding['severity']` union (for example `Record<FrontmatterFinding['severity'], ...>`). The compiler then enforces exhaustiveness, and the `?? '?'` and the string compare can go.

findings.title: Fix-log lookup is O(n·m) and keyed by file and field
findings.description: `fixLog.find(...)` runs per finding. That is fine at this scale. If a file ever has two findings on the same field, the second would show the first one's before/after. A `Map` keyed by `filePath + field`, or a `fixResult` attached to each finding, would remove both issues. This is optional.

findings.title: `handleError` exit-code parameter is a sound, minimal change
findings.description: The `exitCode = 1` default preserves existing callers. The doc comment was updated to match. The test "an unresolvable project exits 2" covers the new path.
